summary: Re-tested the public backend and authenticated desktop/mobile UI. Email auth, protected dashboard, barber browsing, canonical booking payload, automatic agenda navigation, payment, history management actions, mobile logout, and logout session clearing passed.

integration_issues.issue: Login redirects to the Google provider, but the frontend has no session_id hash parsing or call to /api/auth/google/session. A valid provider callback will return to the root and remain on the login screen.

action_items: Implement the Google callback flow in App.js: read session_id from window.location.hash, exchange it through /api/auth/google/session, and clear the hash after success/failure.
critical_code_review_comments: Google login currently has only the outbound redirect; there is no callback/session exchange implementation despite the backend endpoint and auth playbook requirement.
The authenticated useEffect fetches barbers and appointments without catch/error UI, so a later API failure can leave the dashboard silently empty.
seed_data_creation: Used the configured test account and created temporary appointments through the real booking flow; no mocked APIs or provider credentials were used.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All email-auth booking/payment/history/mobile flows passed. Invalid Google session returns 401 and MongoDB _id is omitted. Retest a real Google provider callback after implementing frontend hash exchange.
rca of the issue: App.js defines only the Google outbound redirect. Neither App.js nor index.js searches window.location.hash for session_id, calls /api/auth/google/session, or sets the authenticated user from the callback response, so the provider's return cannot establish a session.
